newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE steady, supply pressure seen in Sept.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE steady, supply pressure seen in Sept.

text.p: Spot MTBE prices held firm in moderate activity on Friday although the any month values were seen strengthening amid concern over plant turnarounds in September.
"There is no more backwardation in the market. Some people were trying to keep it but supply looks like it will be tight again in September," said a U.S. Gulf trader.
For the past two weeks traders had been predicting a price ease in mid-August, when imports were to resume to normal levels and U.S. production would have been at normal operating rates.

But an unconfirmed turnaround at Texas Petrochemicals Corp 19,000 bpd Texas plant and at ARCO Chemical's 20,000 bpd plant are likely to stress supply. The turnarounds combined with an already announced scheduled turnaround in September at Alberta Enviro Fuels 15,000 bpd plant in Canada and technical problems at the 16,000 bpd SADAF plant in Saudi Arabia.
About 70 percent of the material from the recently launched SADAF plant was expected to be marketed in the U.S., according to industry players.
In the Gulf, prompt August deals were heard done at 94.00 cents and 94.50 cents, with any month barrels seen in the same range of 94.50/95.00 cents.
In the New York Harbor, the range held at 99.00/100.00 a gallon.
Traders said there were at least three trading houses and producers currently loading or about to load ships in the U.S. Gulf for shipment to the Harbor to meet demand by blenders.
